question: Should OpenClaw support a reachable non-loopback private-ingress no-auth Gateway mode, and if so what explicit unsafe acknowledgement or deployment guard should be required?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally weakens a stable Gateway auth/security boundary, so code inspection cannot decide whether trusted external infrastructure should be accepted as the product contract.

options.title: Guarded private-ingress opt-in
options.body: Approve a deliberately named unsafe/private-ingress mode or flag with warnings, audit coverage, docs, and tests for both CLI and runtime startup.

options.title: Keep fail-closed boundary
options.body: Continue requiring token/password or trusted-proxy auth for non-loopback binds and close this direction as not planned after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Raw auth.mode none exemption
options.body: Allow existing auth.mode="none" to bypass non-loopback startup guards without a separate acknowledgement, accepting the unauthenticated exposure risk.

recommendation.title: Guarded private-ingress opt-in
recommendation.body: Approve a deliberately named unsafe/private-ingress mode or flag with warnings, audit coverage, docs, and tests for both CLI and runtime startup.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete appears in recent merge/review history for the trusted-proxy and exposed-startup hardening boundary this decision would change.
